title: Analysis of scenarios and Stress test
heading: 1.2.1.2.6 Analysis of scenarios and Stress test
start_phrase: The quantitative measurement framework is the basis for integrating climate risk in both capital requirements and the severely adverse scenario for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP).
summary:
- Describes the bank’s quantitative framework for integrating climate risk into capital requirements and the ICAAP severely adverse scenario.
- Notes first-time inclusion (Dec 2023 reference date) of capital requirements for climate risk in ICAAP, using adverse scenarios: “orderly transition” for transition risk and “Hot House World” for physical risk, reflecting a conservative stance.
- Confirms a 3-year ICAAP horizon aligned with financial planning and stress testing methodologies.
- Concludes that climate risks have an immaterial impact on economic capital.
- Extends the methodology to quantify exposures affecting liquidity risk, incorporating the impact into the ILAAP.
- Reports CaixaBank’s participation (end-2023 to early-2024) in the EBA’s one-off Fit‑for‑55 climate risk scenario analysis assessing system-wide resilience and support for the green transition under stress (baseline, AD1, AD2).
- Summarizes EBA results (disclosed end‑2024): transition risk losses alone do not threaten financial stability, but could rise notably when combined with macroeconomic stress; major institutions are well capitalized, diversified, and able to hedge/absorb losses.
- Details scenario design: Baseline implements Fit‑for‑55 (55% emissions cut by 2030 vs. 1990 and net zero by 2050) with immediate transition costs (3.7 billion euros energy investments 2022–2030 and a 14.5 pp reduction in fossil fuel consumption); AD1 adds a sudden “run‑on‑brown” asset price correction; AD2 layers in macroeconomic stress akin to EBA stress tests.
text:
Analysis of scenarios and Stress test
The quantitative measurement framework is the basis for integrating climate risk 
in both capital requirements and the severely adverse scenario for the Internal 
Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP). 
In this context, the ICAAP with reference date December 2023 included for the 
first time the estimate of capital requirements due to climate risk. The most 
adverse scenarios available were employed to estimate it. For transition risk , a 
scenario of "orderly transition", which involves a gradual but unavoidable 
process of decarbonisation, was used. However, in the physical risk , the "Hot 
House World” scenario was employed. This scenario considers a significant rise 
of the global temperatures due to a lack of climatic action, causing extreme 
events that are more intense and frequent. This selection prioritises preparing 
the Entity against complex scenarios.
The time horizon used in the ICAAP is of 3 years. This time horizon is coherent 
with the framework for financial planning and stress tests, as the methodology is 
also based on the analysis of scenarios. This selection, together with the 
selection of more adverse scenarios, is inline with a conservative approach.
The analysis concluded that the impact of climate risks on the economic capital is 
immaterial.
This methodology has also allowed quantifying the exposure potentially affected 
by climate risk with an impact on liquidity risk, where this impact has been 
included in the ILAAP. Furthermore, between the end of 2023 and early 2024, CaixaBank participated in 
the one-off analysis of the Fit-for-55 climate risk scenario carried out by the EBA. 
The aim of the exercise was to assess the resilience of the EU's financial system 
(including banks, insurers, IORP and investment funds) against the potential 
impact of climate risks under three different stress scenarios (baseline, AD1 and 
AD21), as well as its capacity to support the ecological transition even under 
stress conditions. The results of this analysis were disclosed at the end of 2024, 
concluding that the losses associated with the transition risk alone are not a 
threat to financial stability, although it should be considered that combined with 
macroeconomic stress, these losses could rise considerably. In addition, the 
financial institutions, particularly the major ones, are well capitalised, their 
exposure is appropriately diversified and they have an adequate capacity for 
hedging and absorbing losses.
1 Baseline: The Fit-for-55 plan is implemented (by 2030, 55% reduction of emissions compared to 1990 levels and NZ in 2050). 
Immediate transition costs are assumed: energy-related investments amounting to 3.7 billion euros between 2022 and 2030 and 
a reduction of 14.5 pp in fossil fuel consumption. In addition to the baseline, AD1 (run-on-brown) considers a sudden correction 
in financial asset prices as a consequence of a greater awareness of transition risks. In addition to AD1, AD2 considers a 
macroeconomic similar to that considered in the EBA stress tests.
                                                                                                                                                                                              Management Report 2024
263

title: Impact of climate change on the Financial Statements - Introduction
heading: 1.3 Impact of climate change on the Financial Statements
start_phrase: As previously mentioned, CaixaBank is exposed to risks associated with climate change mainly via the financing of sectors exposed to extreme weather or those more intensive in CO2 emissions.
summary: Overview of how climate change risks may affect CaixaBank’s financial statements: exposure arises via financing sectors vulnerable to extreme weather or high CO2 emissions, potentially weakening households’ and companies’ payment capacity, savings, and investment. Identified income statement impacts include lower net interest income (from reduced investment capacity) and higher allowances for insolvency risk (due to losses, including diminished collateral/guarantee values), which could slightly reduce capital adequacy ratios through higher provisions and lower returns. Despite these risks, CaixaBank’s scenario analysis within its risk measurement and monitoring framework indicates limited impacts on the lending portfolio for both transition and physical risks. Management actions include customer engagement and transition action plans, portfolio mix adjustments to reduce exposure, and financing opportunities tied to climate adaptation.
text:
Impact of climate change on the Financial Statements
As previously mentioned, CaixaBank is exposed to risks associated with climate 
change mainly via the financing of sectors exposed to extreme weather or those 
more intensive in CO2 emissions.
These risks could have an impact on the financial sector, to the extent that they 
lead to changes in the financial situation of households and companies and they 
also affect their capacity to meet their payment commitments or their savings 
and investment capacity.
Therefore, it has been identified that the risks associated with climate change 
could have an impact on the Group's financial statements in the future. 
Specifically, financial effects that would have an impact on the following items of 
the income statement have been identified:
> Net interest income.  The impact that the physical and transition climate 
risks could have on the investment capacity of households and companies 
could result in CaixaBank generating less net income. 
> Allowances for insolvency risk.  The materialisation of risk climates can 
have a direct impact on the financial situation of households and companies, 
which affect their capacity to meet their payment commitments. These 
events can generate economic losses, for example, via the value of the 
guarantees. This leads to an increase in allowances for insolvency risk.
Consequently, the mentioned impacts could involve a slight reduction in the 
capital adequacy ratios derived from the increase of allowances for insolvency 
risk and the lower generation of net income and business returns.
However, in spite of the identification of the aforementioned potential financial 
impacts on the Group, the results obtained after conducting the scenario 
analysis within CaixaBank's framework for measurement and monitoring show 
limited impacts on the lending portfolio in both terms of transition and physical 
risk.
CaixaBank monitors these risks in detail, with the aim of minimising their effect, 
and has management tools in place to manage the impact thereof:> Implementation of action plans to help these companies transition. ä See 
section “ Engagement with customers” .
> Change in the portfolio mix, in order to readjust the exposure to these risks.
> Financing of new business opportunity linked to the adaptation of these 
sectors to climate change.

title: Impact on the net interest income
heading: 1.3.1 Impact on the net interest income
start_phrase: A negative impact on the net interest income caused by the climate risk is not expected in the medium/short term.
summary:
- The document analyzes how climate change risks could affect CaixaBank’s financial statements, primarily through exposure to high CO2-emitting and weather-sensitive sectors.
- It explains that climate risks may weaken households’ and companies’ financial positions, potentially impacting their payment capacity, savings, and investment, which in turn affects the bank.
- Identified income statement impacts:
  - Net interest income: potential reduction if clients’ investment capacity declines.
  - Allowances for insolvency risk: potential increase due to higher credit risk and collateral value losses from climate-related events.
- These effects could slightly reduce capital adequacy ratios via higher provisions and lower earnings.
- Scenario analysis within CaixaBank’s risk framework indicates limited impact on the lending portfolio from both transition and physical risks.
- Risk management measures include:
  - Action plans and customer engagement to support transition.
  - Adjusting the portfolio mix toward lower-risk, less GHG-intensive exposures (aligned with NZBA commitments).
  - Financing opportunities tied to adaptation and the energy transition to diversify income.
- Net interest income outlook: no negative impact expected in the short/medium term due to portfolio flexibility and growth in sustainable finance.
- Provisions methodology: downside scenarios incorporate macro effects consistent with exacerbated climate risk (e.g., higher production and commodity costs leading to lower productivity and GDP).
- Scenario weightings used for Spain and Portugal across 2022–2024 are stable at 60% baseline, 20% upside, 20% downside.
text:
Impact on the net interest income
A negative impact on the net interest income caused by the climate risk is not 
expected in the medium/short term. CaixaBank has the capacity to adjust its 
portfolio mix to fit the circumstances. In this case the adherence to the NZBA will 
involve a change in the portoflio mix, focusing on less GHG intensive customers 
and operations. In addition, the Group is committed to supporting its customers 
in the transition to a carbon-neutral economy. The Entity also has the 
opportunity of making the most of the growing demand in sustainable finance, 
which would enable it to diversify its investments in projects that promote the 
energy transition and sustainable development, generating new sources of 
income. 
This flexibility and approach in sustainability contribute to mitigating the possible 
negative impacts of climate risks on its profitability.

title: Impact on the calculation of allowances for insolvency risk
heading: 1.3.2 Impact on the calculation of allowances for insolvency risk
start_phrase: The downside range of variables used to calculate provisions includes deficiencies in structural reforms leading —together with other macroeconomic dynamics— to drops in productivity and thus in GDP.
summary:
- Focus: How climate change risks could affect CaixaBank’s financial statements.
- Risk channels: Exposure through financing of sectors vulnerable to extreme weather and high CO2 emissions, which can weaken household and corporate finances, repayment capacity, savings, and investment.
- Income statement impacts identified:
  - Net interest income: Potentially lower if clients’ investment capacity declines.
  - Allowances for insolvency risk: Likely higher due to deteriorated borrower solvency and reduced collateral values when climate risks materialize.
- Capital effects: Slight potential reduction in capital adequacy ratios from higher provisions and lower net income/returns.
- Scenario analysis outcome: Internal assessments indicate limited impact on the lending portfolio from both transition and physical risks.
- Risk management and mitigation:
  - Action plans and engagement to support client transition (NZBA commitment).
  - Portfolio rebalancing toward less GHG‑intensive clients and sectors.
  - Financing opportunities tied to adaptation and the energy transition, leveraging growing sustainable finance demand.
- Net interest income outlook: No negative impact expected in the short-to-medium term due to portfolio flexibility, client transition support, and diversification into sustainable projects.
- Provisions methodology: Downside scenarios incorporate structural reform shortfalls and macro dynamics (e.g., higher production and commodity costs) that depress productivity and GDP, reflecting exacerbated climate risk pathways.
- Scenario weightings used for provisioning (Spain and Portugal): Baseline 60%, Upside 20%, Downside 20% for 2022, 2023, and 2024.
text:
Impact on the calculation of allowances for insolvency risk
The downside range of variables used to calculate provisions includes 
deficiencies in structural reforms leading —together with other macroeconomic 
dynamics— to drops in productivity and thus in GDP. Thus, the estimated drop 
reflects the potential impact of an exacerbated climate risk which, through 
various mechanisms (e.g., increased production costs, increased commodity 
prices, etc.), would eventually affect long-term economic growth. The weighting

title: Integration of climate change in the management systems
heading: 1.4.1 Integration of climate change in the management systems
start_phrase: The physical and transition risks associated with climate change are considered additional factors that have an impact on the previously defined risk categories, and their identification, measurement, management and monitoring are completely integrated into the Entity's risk management framework.
summary:
- Climate change risks (physical and transition) are fully integrated into the Entity’s risk management framework, governance processes, policies, and strategic planning, including the risk catalogue, risk appetite framework, and risk assessments.
- Climate risk metrics are embedded in monitoring and reporting, with key indicators included in the risk appetite framework.
- Ongoing monitoring covers: portfolio concentration in carbon‑intensive corporate sectors; financed emissions; decarbonisation metrics aligned with NZBA targets; and mobilisation of sustainable finance.
- Additional tracked aspects include: exposures to transition risk by intensive sector; energy efficiency of the mortgage portfolio; banking book exposures to the top 20 global carbon‑intensive firms; and exposures subject to physical risk (with a correction noted on October 31, 2024).
text:
Integration of climate change in the management systems
The physical and transition risks associated with climate change are considered 
additional factors that have an impact on the previously defined risk categories, 
and their identification, measurement, management and monitoring are 
completely integrated into the Entity's risk management framework. Therefore, 
the risks related to climate change are incorporated into the implemented 
governance processes and models, in accordance with regulations and 
supervisory trends.
The Entity's management of risks associated with climate change is part of the 
risk planning, corporate strategic processes, risk catalogue, risk appetite 
framework and risk assessment, and it is established in the risk management 
policies, frameworks and risks processes.

title: Climate strategy - Introduction
heading: 1.6 Climate strategy
start_phrase: Below is presented the CaixaBank Group's climate strategy.
summary: Overview of CaixaBank Group’s climate strategy, positioned within its broader sustainability agenda (one of three strategic priorities) and aligned with the 2022–2024 Sustainable Banking Plan and the new 2025–2027 Sustainability Plan. It targets contributing to a carbon‑neutral, more sustainable economy by financing and investing in sustainable projects, managing climate risk, and reducing the impact of operations. The Group is developing a Climate Transition Plan to be completed within the 2025–2027 timeframe; its pillars are decarbonisation targets and sectoral transition plans, a solid governance model, and policies guiding implementation. The strategy is informed by a framework for identifying, assessing, and measuring climate‑related risks and will be executed through two lines of action (not detailed here).
text:
Climate strategy
Below is presented the CaixaBank Group's climate strategy. This strategy can be 
impacted by  risks and opportunities related to the climate. This is why, 
CaixaBank has established a framework for identifying, assessing and measuring 
risks, which has been explained in previous sections.
As mentioned in the section “ Sustainability Strategy ”, CaixaBank has defined 
sustainability as one of its three strategic priorities. The Group's sustainability 
strategy is set out in the 2022-2024 Sustainable Banking Plan.
Driving the sustainable transition of companies and society is one of the three 
ambitions of this Sustainable Banking Plan and the new 2025-2027 Sustainability 
Plan. The Group has a climate strategy that must contribute to the transition to a 
carbon-neutral and more sustainable economy by financing and investing in 
sustainable projects, managing climate risk and curbing the impact of its 
operations. 
The CaixaBank Group continues to advance in the development of its Climate 
Transition Plan, which is expected to be completed within the timeframe of the 
2025-2027 Sustainability Plan. The Climate Transition Plan will reflect the Group's 
strategy for climate change, and its pillars are the main elements of the current 
climate strategy, which are the Group's decarbonisation targets and the sectoral 
transition plans, a solid governance model and the policies guiding its 
implementation. These pillars ensure a coherent and effective integration of the 
action plans followed.

title: Objective 02. Achieve zero net emissions by 2050 ( Net Zero )
heading: 1.6.2 Objective 02. Achieve zero net emissions by 2050 ( Net Zero )
start_phrase: CaixaBank's ambition is to achieve zero net emission by 2050 and promote the company's decarbonisation arrive at the neutrality in issuances of carbon for 2050 and promote society's decarbonisation.
summary:
- Objective: Achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 and drive decarbonisation across CaixaBank and society.
- Strategy built on three lines of action:
  1) Align investment and lending portfolios with the Paris Agreement to limit warming to 1.5°C, setting 2030 interim decarbonisation targets in key sectors in line with NZBA and NZAOA.
  2) Reduce the bank’s direct operational footprint through eight pillars defined in the 2022–2024 Environmental Management Plan.
  3) Support clients’ transition with tailored solutions based on their decarbonisation maturity.
- Additional commitment: Evaluate introducing an internal carbon pricing system within the 2025–2027 Sustainability Plan.
text:
CaixaBank's ambition is to achieve zero net emission by 2050 and promote the 
company's decarbonisation arrive at the neutrality in issuances of carbon for 
2050 and promote society's decarbonisation. With this objective in mind, 
CaixaBank has developed a strategy with three lines of action: 
1. Align the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement targets in 
order to contribute to limiting global warming to an increase of 1.5ºC above 
pre-industrial levels, setting interim decarbonisation targets for 2030 in 
certain sectors, in line with the NZBA and Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance 
(NZAOA).
2. The global strategy for minimising direct impacts in CaixaBank's own 
operations (operational footprint) is based around 8 main pillars, defined in 
the 2022-2024 Environmental Management Plan. 
3. Support for businesses (customers and emitters). CaixaBank provides its 
customers with solutions aimed at helping them in the transition towards 
net zero emissions, which are based on the customer's degree of 
advancement in its path towards decarbonisation.
Within the framework of CaixaBank's commitment to aligning its 
activity to the Paris Agreement and reducing direct and indirect 
emissions, it undertakes to analyse the suitability of applying a 
system for setting an internal price for carbon, within the scope of

title: Alignment of the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement - Introduction
heading: 1.6.3 Alignment of the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement
start_phrase: In order to meet the objective of carbon neutral emissions by 2050, CaixaBank has focused on the decarbonisation of the Group's investment and credit portfolio, emphasising on the more carbon intensive1 sectors through its commitment to the NZBA and NZAOA.
summary: Introduction describing CaixaBank’s strategy to align its investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement, targeting carbon neutrality by 2050 and a 1.5°C pathway by focusing on high-emitting sectors via commitments to NZBA and NZAOA. It notes CaixaBank as a founding NZBA member (UNEP FI, April 2021) with obligations to set science-based, interim decarbonization targets, and that VidaCaixa joined NZAOA in 2022 as the first Spanish insurer/pension manager. The text highlights inclusion of financed (client) emissions, intent to publish interim targets for the most intensive sectors per UNEP FI Target-Setting Guidelines, and ongoing work to reconcile NZBA requirements with SBTi standards to avoid duplicating objectives.
text:
Alignment of the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement 
In order to meet the objective of carbon neutral emissions by 2050, CaixaBank 
has focused on the decarbonisation of the Group's investment and credit 
portfolio, emphasising on the more carbon intensive1 sectors through its 
commitment to the NZBA and NZAOA.
Signing the NZBA and NZAOA involves aligning the investment and credit 
portfolio with the Paris Agreement2 targets to contribute to limiting the 
temperature increase by 1.5ºC with respect to pre-industrial levels.
In April 2021, CaixaBank signed, as a founding member, 
the NZBA promoted by the UNEP FI, by means of which 
it commits to achieving net zero emissions and setting 
intermediate decarbonisation targets. Furthermore, in 2022  
VidaCaixa was the first insurance company and pension 
fund manager in Spain to join the NZAOA.
Currently, NZBA is the benchmark standard for setting decarbonisation targets in 
the banking sector and commits the Bank to setting science-based targets. 
However, aware that SBTi (Science Based Targets initiative) is the reference 
standard for the non-financial sectors, the Bank has initiatives underway to 
assess how to reconcile the two standards without duplicating objectives and 
efforts. Within the NZBA working group, led by UNEP FI and of which CaixaBank 
is a member, work is underway to resolve these issues and determine next 
steps.As mentioned above, the commitment “Zero Emissions by 2050” of the NZBA 
also includes the emissions of customers receiving Bank funding (credit 
portfolio). To accompany clients in the transition towards a more sustainable 
future, with specific plans and targets, CaixaBank committed to publish interim 
targets for the most intensive sectors indicated in the UNEP FI Guidelines for 
Target Setting and prioritising, among these, the most relevant in the CaixaBank 
portfolio.

title: NZBA decarbonisation targets
heading: 1.6.3.1 NZBA decarbonisation targets
start_phrase: Within the framework of the NZBA, CaixaBank published its first decarbonisation targets3 for 2030 for the electricity generation and oil and gas sectors in October 2022.
summary:
- Objective: Align CaixaBank’s investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement to reach net-zero by 2050, prioritizing carbon‑intensive sectors through NZBA and NZAOA commitments.
- Alliances and governance: Founding member of NZBA (2021); VidaCaixa joined NZAOA (2022). NZBA is used to set science‑based targets; CaixaBank is working within UNEP FI to reconcile NZBA with SBTi and avoid duplications.
- Scope of commitment: Includes financed emissions from clients (credit portfolio). Interim targets set for priority, high‑emitting sectors per UNEP FI guidance, covering CaixaBank, S.A. and Banco BPI; prioritized sectors represent over 43.8% of total corporate and project finance exposure.
- Methodology and controls: Financed emissions calculated under PCAF’s Global GHG Accounting Standard and externally audited. Target scopes tailored by sector materiality across Scopes 1–3, value‑chain stages, and relevant metrics (absolute, economic, physical). Subject to the Group’s three lines of defence. Pathways generally aligned to 1.5°C scenarios.
- Target‑setting progress: 
  - 2022: First 2030 targets for electricity generation and oil & gas.
  - 2023: Added thermal coal, iron & steel, and automotive.
  - 2024: Added commercial and residential real estate, maritime, aviation, and agriculture & livestock; aluminium and cement deemed non‑material (monitoring only).
- Baselines and ambition: Baseline years chosen for data availability and representativeness (e.g., oil & gas 2020, acknowledging COVID-19 effects makes ambition stronger). CaixaBank will maintain reduction ambition even if baselines or methodologies evolve.
- 2030 sector targets (high level):
  - Power generation: −30% physical intensity (to 95 kg CO2e/MWh).
  - Oil & gas (fossil fuel combustion/financed emissions): −23% absolute emissions.
  - Automotive: −33% Scope 3 intensity (gCO2/vkm).
  - Iron & steel: −10% to −20% Scope 1+2 intensity (kg CO2e/t).
  - Thermal coal: 100% exit from exposure.
  - Commercial real estate: −41% intensity (CRREM 1.5°C Iberia).
  - Residential real estate: −19% intensity (CRREM 1.5°C Spain/Portugal).
  - Maritime: reduce alignment delta to 0% (IMO method).
  - Aviation: −30% intensity (gCO2e/RPK, MPPU 1.5°).
  - Agriculture & livestock: qualitative target focused on improving data and client/sector profiling (SBTi FLAG).
- Notes and disclosures: Commercial real estate and maritime targets are noted elsewhere as not aligned with a 1.5°C pathway. No activities incompatible with a climate‑neutral transition identified. CaixaBank is not excluded from EU‑Paris benchmarks due to its business nature but will disclose exposures to companies excluded from those indices in its March 2025 prudential report. Targets are based on best practices and stakeholder input but are not independently assured.
text:
NZBA decarbonisation targets
Within the framework of the NZBA, CaixaBank published its first decarbonisation 
targets3 for 2030 for the electricity generation and oil and gas sectors in October 
2022. In 2023, it published the targets for the thermal coal, iron and steel and 
automotive sectors. 
Lastly, in April 2024 CaixaBank published 2030 decarbonisation targets for five 
new sectors: real estate (residential and commercial), maritime, aviation and 
agriculture and livestock. Furthermore, it has determined the non-materiality of 
the aluminium and cement portfolio. These are sectors for which a portfolio 
monitoring strategy has been established. 
By publishing these latest targets, CaixaBank has completed the phase of setting 
decarbonisation targets for 2030 for the sectors prioritised (carbon-intensive 
sectors) by the NZBA commitment. These goals have been established for the 
exposure of the loan and investment portfolio of CaixaBank, S.A. and Banco BPI, 
and they account for more than 43.8%  of total corporate finance and project 
finance.
1 Given the nature of CaixaBank's business, no commercial activities or assets incompatible with a transition to a climate neutral 
economy have been identified.
2 CaixaBank is not excluded from the EU-Paris benchmark indices due to not applying exclusion criteria, on account of the nature 
of its business. However, in the Information of Prudential Relevance that CaixaBank will publish on 28 March 2025, it will include 
in section 8.4.1 in template 1: "Banking book - Climate change transition risk: credit quality of exposures by sector, emissions and 
residual maturity" the exposures to companies excluded from said indices in accordance with article, 12, section 1, letters d) to g) 
and section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1818.
3 The targets have not been reviewed by an independent third party. These targets have been set considering the best market 
practices and the opinions of the main stakeholders, as they are targets based on science and aligned with that established in 
the guide for setting targets by UNEP-FI.                                                                                                                                                                                              Management Report 2024
270
The decarbonisation targets have been determined based on the best available 
practices and in line with the requirements of NZBA. Data on emissions financed, 
used to determine the baseline and reported each year ( ä	 see section " 
Transition plans and alignment "), follow the methodology developed by PCAF and 
described in the standard  "The Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard 
for the Financial Industry" and are externally audited ( ä	see section " Calculation 
of financed CO2 emissions ”). In order to determine the scope of decarbonisation 
targets, the types of emissions (Scope 1, 2, or 3), stages in the value chain of the 
sector (upstream, midstream, or downstream), and the most relevant metrics 
(absolute emissions, economic intensity, or physical intensity) are considered to 
decarbonise CaixaBank's portfolio. That is, the process for selecting the 
decarbonisations targets and scopes for each sector has consisted in identifying 
each segment's economic and emissions materiality in order to focus efforts on 
the phases of the value chain on which the most impact can be made. The 
idiosyncrasies of counterparts has been considered in some sectors in order to 
also exclude them from the scope of the decarbonisation targets. Thus, in spite 
of the scopes and sectors of the data reported in the financed emissions being 
different from those used in the decarbonisation targets, the best practices 
promoted by the NZBA are met and they are subject to the internal control 
model of the CaixaBank Group's 3 lines of defence. 
All the decarbonisation pathways have considered scenarios that limit the 
increase of global temperature to 1.5ºC, as set forth in the Paris 
Agreement1.
The baseline year for the decarbonisation targets has been selected according to 
the availability of data. They are considered to be representative in terms of the 
activities covered and the influences of external factors. In fact, as regards the oil 
and gas sectors, the baseline year (2020) could be influenced by the COVID-19 
pandemic, which is when the sector's total emissions dropped due to a lower 
global economic activity. Thus, by selecting 2020 as the baseline year for this 
sector's decarbonisation target, if anything, makes the target even more 
ambitious. Furthermore, setting the target to 2030 involves considering the 
alignment objectives of the main customers and the expectations of changes in 
consumer preferences, the development of new technologies and other 
regulatory adjustments that can be used as levers to achieve their climate 
objectives.
1 As indicated in the section “ Transition plans and alignment ”, the targets set for the commercial real estate and naval 
sectors are not aligned with the pathway of 1.5ºC.
                                                                                                                                                                                              Management Report 2024

title: NZAOA decarbonisation targets
heading: 1.6.3.2 NZAOA decarbonisation targets
start_phrase: As part of the NZAOA initiative, VidaCaixa has set intermediate decarbonisation targets (to 2030) for the CaixaBank Group's insurance business, focusing on three areas:
summary:
- VidaCaixa, under the NZAOA initiative, sets 2030 interim decarbonisation targets for CaixaBank Group’s insurance business across three fronts: portfolio emissions reduction, climate-focused corporate dialogues, and transition finance.
- Portfolio emissions target: cut the scopes 1 and 2 carbon footprint intensity of corporate investments by at least 50% by 2030 versus a 2019 baseline of 177 tCO2 per million euros invested; establish rolling five-year targets after 2030 to reach net zero by 2050 at the latest.
- Target-setting is aligned with the NZAOA protocol and a 1.5°C IPCC “no or limited overshoot” pathway; the 2020–2030 reduction threshold of 40–60% is set at the median 50%.
- Offsetting is not allowed in setting targets for scope 3.15 under the current NZAOA framework; potential long-term use may be considered only after minimizing the carbon footprint.
- Climate stewardship: engage at least 20 carbon‑intensive companies (or those responsible for 65% of portfolio emissions) to improve their climate targets, leveraging channels such as Climate Action 100+ and contributing to alliance-led decarbonisation reports.
- Transition finance: actively support the energy transition via climate-positive instruments, including green bonds (e.g., for energy efficiency) and thematic climate funds.
- Governance: NZBA decarbonisation targets are approved by the Board; cross-functional groups meet weekly to track operations affecting NZBA metrics; monthly updates go to the Sustainability and Global Risk Committees; annual reporting to the Management Committee, the Appointments and Sustainability Committee, and the Risks Committee.
- Monitoring and integration: VidaCaixa regularly tracks exposure to carbon‑intensive sectors and portfolio carbon footprint, incorporates climate metrics and ESG assessments into investment decisions, and reports significant progress in reducing the insurance investment portfolio’s carbon footprint.
text:
NZAOA decarbonisation targets  
As part of the NZAOA initiative, VidaCaixa has set intermediate decarbonisation targets (to 2030) for the CaixaBank Group's insurance business, focusing on three 
areas:
Emission reduction targets in the portfolio: VidaCaixa has established the 
target of cutting the carbon footprint (scopes 1 and 2) of corporate 
investments by at least 50% by 2030, compared to 2019. The baseline year's 
value is 177 tCO2/M EUR invested. As of 2030, targets will be set every five 
years until reaching net zero emissions, which must be by 2050 the latest. 
The emission reduction targets are set according to the alliance's protocol, 
which establishes thresholds aligned with the science. For example, the 
reduction threshold for the 2020-2030 period must be set at between 40% 
and 60%, which is why VidaCaixa has set the reduction target as the 
threshold's median value, at 50%. 
The scenario selected to define the decarbonisation targets in the alliance's 
protocol is 1.5ºC of the IPCC (‘no or limited overshoot’). As regards scope 3.15 
within the framework of the NZAOA targets, offsetting mechanisms are 
currently not permitted as a way to calculate the decarbonisation targets, 
although the role of offsetting may be considered in the long term, once the 
carbon footprint has been reduced to minimum levels.
Climate dialogues: VidaCaixa will engage in dialogues with at least 20 carbon-
intensive companies (or those responsible for 65% of emissions in the 
portfolio) in order to improve their climate targets and maintain other 
channels of dialogue on climate issues (through leadership in partnership 
dialogues in the framework of the Climate Action 100+ initiative). Additionally, 
VidaCaixa is involved in preparing reports relevant to decarbonisation 
promoted by the alliance or similar.Financing the transition: VidaCaixa will take an active role in financing the 
energy transition through financing instruments for climate-positive 
solutions, such as projects to enhance energy efficiency through green bonds 
or investment in thematic climate funds.

title: Governance of decarbonisation targets
heading: 1.6.3.3 Governance of decarbonisation targets
start_phrase: The set NZBA decarbonisation targets have been approved by the Board of Directors.
summary:
- VidaCaixa, under the NZAOA initiative, sets 2030 interim decarbonisation targets for CaixaBank Group’s insurance business across three pillars: portfolio emissions cuts, climate-focused corporate engagement, and transition financing.
- Portfolio emissions target: reduce scopes 1 and 2 carbon footprint of corporate investments by at least 50% by 2030 versus a 2019 baseline of 177 tCO2 per million euros invested; reset targets every five years to reach net zero by 2050 at the latest.
- Targets align with NZAOA protocol and science-based thresholds (40–60% reduction for 2020–2030; VidaCaixa adopts the 50% midpoint) and use the IPCC 1.5°C “no/limited overshoot” scenario.
- Offsetting is not permitted for setting NZAOA decarbonisation targets (including scope 3.15); the role of offsets may be reconsidered long term once residual emissions are minimized.
- Climate dialogues: engage with at least 20 carbon‑intensive companies or those responsible for 65% of portfolio emissions; leverage initiatives like Climate Action 100+ and contribute to alliance-led decarbonisation reports.
- Transition financing: proactively fund climate‑positive solutions (e.g., green bonds for energy efficiency, thematic climate funds).
- Governance: decarbonisation targets (referred to as NZBA in the governance section) approved by the Board; cross‑functional groups meet weekly to review operations affecting metrics; monthly reporting to the Sustainability and Global Risk Committees; annual updates to the Management, Appointments & Sustainability, and Risks Committees.
- Ongoing monitoring of exposure to carbon‑intensive sectors and portfolio carbon footprint, integrating climate metrics and ESG assessments into investment decisions, leading to significant reductions in the insurance investment portfolio’s carbon footprint.
text:
Governance of decarbonisation targets 
The set NZBA decarbonisation targets  have been approved by the Board of 
Directors. In order to monitor the alignment objectives of the sectors for which 
these targets have been set and to oversee their fulfilment:
> Groups have been created for the various business areas that meet on a 
weekly basis to review the operations with an impact on the NZBA metrics in 
accordance with annual management goals. The groups include to members 
from the areas of Environmental Risk Approval, Risk Management Function 
and Business and Climate Risk.
> A progress report on the main NZBA metrics is presented to the 
Sustainability Committee and the Global Risk Committee on a monthly basis.
> On a yearly basis, the Management Committee, the Appointments and 
Sustainability Committee and the Risks Committee are reported on the 
evolution of these metrics. 
VidaCaixa has different mechanisms that enable it to regularly monitor exposure 
to carbon-intensive sectors of activity and the carbon footprint of its 
investments. In analysing these climate metrics and assessing the ESG quality of 
the companies invested in (through rating or specific material factors for each 
sector) and incorporating them into the investment decision-making process, 
VidaCaixa has made major advances in reducing the carbon footprint of the 
insurance investment portfolio.                                                                                                                                                                                                 Management Report 2024
273

title: Transition plans and alignment - Introduction
heading: 1.6.3.4 Transition plans and alignment
start_phrase: Since setting the first NZBA targets, CaixaBank has been actively managing its sectoral portfolios to ensure that the transition to the targets set for each sector are properly met.
summary: Introduction to CaixaBank’s sectoral transition plans under NZBA, outlining active management of sectoral portfolios and noting that portfolio decarbonisation may be non-linear due to client support. Describes key portfolio alignment actions: measurement and monitoring (maximum emission intensity limits for new operations/customers, CO2 and climate impact assessment of all new transactions, estimating metrics for recent positions by sector, identifying change drivers, and compiling/monitoring customers’ climate transition plans); control and admission policy (risk admission “red lines” via the Sustainability risk policy and reviewing/penalising new operations); and dialogue/engagement (assessing and classifying key customers’ alignment with sustainability indicators, setting improvement strategies, and offering transition-supporting products/services). Acknowledges that decarbonisation outcomes also depend on government policy, regulation, consumer behaviour, scientific advances, and new technologies. Signals that subsequent content details sectoral alignment plans and customer transition progress for all targeted sectors.
text:
Transition plans and alignment
Since setting the first NZBA targets, CaixaBank has been actively managing its 
sectoral portfolios to ensure that the transition to the targets set for each sector 
are properly met. 
However, it is worth noting that CaixaBank's vocation to accompany its 
customers in their transition process as a mechanism to attain the 
decarbonisation of the economy means that the decarbonisation trajectory of 
the portfolio point by point may not be linear. 
In this context, the main actions carried out to manage the portfolio's alignment 
metrics include the following:
Measurement and monitoring
> Setting maximum emission intensity limits for new operations and 
customers.
> Assessment of CO2 emissions and the impact on climate of all new 
transactions.
> Calculation of the estimates of metrics for the most recent positions in the 
portfolio for each sector.
> Identification of the main drivers of the changes. 
> Compile, assess and monitor the climate transition plans published by 
customers.
Control policy and admission policy
> Involving red lines in risk admission through the Sustainability risk policy.
> Review and penalise new operations. 
Dialogue and engagement service
> Assessment and classification of the level of alignment with sustainability 
indicators of the key customers for each sector.
> Setting of strategies to improve the indicators.
> Provision of products and services supporting the transition.
Within this section, further detail is given to the actions specifically carried out 
with customers in each of the objectives for which decarbonisation targets have 
been defined.In spite of all the actions carried out by CaixaBank to support customers in 
defining and executing strategies to transition towards a more sustainable 
model, the success of decarbonisation is also dependant on changes derived 
from government policies and environmental and climatic regulations, as well as 
on changes in consumer behaviour, scientific developments and new 
technologies.
Below are detailed the sectoral alignment plans and the progress made in the 
transition plans of customers for all the sectors in which CaixaBank has set a 
target.

title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
heading: 1.6.3.4.1.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric of 30% has been set, with the following characteristics:
summary:
- Focus and scope: The alignment metric targets the electricity sector, concentrating on the generation segment where decarbonisation has the greatest impact, and includes integrated companies across the value chain. Only Scope 1 emissions are included; Scope 2 is immaterial and Scope 3 is difficult to influence from generation and is covered by other sector targets.
- Metric and reference pathway: Uses a physical emissions intensity metric (kg CO2e/MWh) to enable comparability across different-sized clients and support growth in more efficient groups. The reference pathway is the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE 2050) scenario. Risk considered is exposure (limit granted).
- Baseline performance: 2020 baseline intensity is 136 kg CO2e/MWh, which is lower than most peer disclosures and even below the IEA’s 2030 target metric (~156 kg CO2e/MWh). This reflects CaixaBank’s long-standing financing of renewables, including green bond issuances from 2020 to 2024.
- 2030 target: A 30% reduction from the 2020 baseline, targeting 95 kg CO2e/MWh by 2030, exceeding the IEA’s implied 2030 reduction (-23%).
- Progress and trajectory: The evolution of the metric is favorable though not linear; approximately 78% of the 2030 reduction has already been achieved, with recent intensity around 105 kg CO2e/MWh. The trajectory remains ambitious given the already low baseline relative to the sector’s IEA NZE 2050 benchmark.
- Constraints and context: Further decarbonisation is challenging due to the low starting point and a complex geopolitical environment for the energy sector, yet CaixaBank maintains its ambition to continue leading renewable energy financing.

title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
heading: 1.6.3.4.1.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
start_phrase: For CaixaBank, the ultimate goal of the decarbonisation strategy for its portfolio in the electricity sector is to guide its customers in their transition to a less emission-intensive generation mix, provided that they are committed to sustainability.
summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s sector transition plan centers on decarbonizing its electricity and oil & gas (O&G) portfolios by guiding customers toward lower-emission models and aligning financing with net‑zero pathways.
- Electricity sector approach:
  - Goal: Reduce portfolio emissions intensity by helping customers shift to less emission‑intensive generation mixes.
  - Levers: Increase financing of renewables and engage strategically with clients to provide solutions that meet or accelerate their decarbonization plans.
  - Portfolio management: Consider rebalancing toward lower‑emission clients and derisking or exiting counterparties not committed to a low‑carbon transition.
- Oil & gas sector alignment:
  - Target metric: Absolute emissions metric, reflecting industry expectations; decarbonization driven by energy efficiency and fuel substitution (demand effects).
  - Recent context: 2022 saw a temporary rise in O&G exposure due to energy security/geopolitical factors to ensure short/medium‑term supply, causing potential metric volatility but not altering medium/long‑term decarbonization commitments.
  - Ambition: A 23% reduction target versus 2020 is effectively more ambitious given the atypical baseline conditions.
- Boundary and methodology:
  - Value chain: Upstream (exploration/extraction), downstream (refining, distribution, marketing), and integrated companies; this captures most sector emissions.
  - Emissions scope: Scopes 1, 2, and 3, with scope 3 recognized as highly material for O&G.
  - Standards alignment: Approach aligned with the NZBA Guide, stakeholder expectations, and peer practices; reference pathway is the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE2050).
  - Measurement basis: Absolute emissions calculated using risk drawn down (not risk granted) to avoid over‑attribution, consistent with PCAF and enabling peer comparability.
  - Key design decisions summarized: value chain coverage, full scope (1–3) accounting, absolute emissions metric based on risk drawn down, IEA NZE2050 pathway selection, and risk considered as drawn down.
text:
Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
For CaixaBank, the ultimate goal of the decarbonisation strategy for its portfolio 
in the electricity sector is to guide its customers in their transition to a less 
emission-intensive generation mix, provided that they are committed to 
sustainability. This is the only way to reach a decarbonised electricity sector. 
CaixaBank will therefore help and encourage its customers to curb the emissions 
intensity of their generation mix, which will consequently lead to a fall in its own 
intensity metric.
The main levers for sector decarbonisation relate to the financing of renewable 
energies and engagement with strategic customers in order to provide them 
with solutions that enable them to comply with —or even accelerate— their 
decarbonisation plans
The possibility of rebalancing our portfolio towards less emission-intensive 
customers and, ultimately, the derisking counterparties that are not committed 
to transition to a low-carbon economy is also under consideration.

title: Evolution of the metric
heading: 1.6.3.4.4.2 Evolution of the metric
start_phrase: The reduction observed in the intensity metric in the iron and steel sector is in line with meeting the ambitious target set by 2030.
summary:
- Document scope: CaixaBank’s Management Report 2024 excerpt on sector alignment metrics, targets, and transition actions for high-emitting sectors (iron & steel and thermal coal).
- Iron & steel sector:
  - The portfolio intensity metric (kgCO2e/t steel) has fallen and is on track for the 2030 target, with a reported trend of around -13% since 2022.
  - CaixaBank will continue efforts to reduce this metric through 2030.
  - Transition plan with customers acknowledges decarbonization complexity and applies prudence in portfolio management.
  - Levers include client engagement and portfolio rebalancing.
  - An intermediate ambition compatible with a 1.5°C pathway targets a 10%–20% reduction, with the lower bound aligned to the IEA Net Zero (NZE) arrival level.
- Coal sector (thermal coal) alignment metric:
  - Design centers on a complete phase-out of exposure to thermal coal by 2030, reflecting the sector’s anticipated disappearance and high emissions profile.
  - CaixaBank will cease financing companies related to thermal coal, targeting zero exposure by 2030, in line with IPCC guidance.
  - 2022 baseline exposure: €2,845m; 2030 arrival level: €0 (–100%).
  - Current exposure mainly involves counterparts with mitigating factors (financing restricted to energy transition purposes or clients with their own pre‑2030 phase-out commitments).
  - Up to 2030, CaixaBank will continue financing activities that support the energy transition and customers executing credible exit strategies from thermal coal.
  - Exposure definition: companies whose economic group derives more than 5% of revenues from thermal coal.

title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
heading: 1.6.3.4.4.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
start_phrase: CaixaBank acknowledges the difficulty implicit in the decarbonisation of this sector, which leads it to consider a certain level of prudence in terms of the management margin for decarbonising the portfolio.
summary:
- Iron and steel sector: CaixaBank reports a decline in its intensity metric, moving toward its 2030 target. The metric fell about 13%, from 1,141 kgCO2e/t steel in 2022 to 984 in 2023, and the bank will continue reducing it through 2030. Its approach includes customer engagement and portfolio rebalancing to pursue an intermediate target compatible with a 1.5 °C pathway, reflecting a 10–20% reduction ambition aligned with IEA Net Zero assumptions at the lower bound. The bank recognizes decarbonization challenges and adopts a prudent management margin while leveraging customer ambition as a key driver.

- Coal sector: CaixaBank sets a full phase-out of thermal coal exposure by 2030, ceasing to finance companies related to thermal coal and reducing exposure to zero. Baseline exposure in 2022 was €2,845m, with a 2030 arrival level of €0 (-100%). Current exposure mainly involves counterparts with mitigating factors: financing limited to energy transition activities or clients that have their own thermal coal phase-out commitments before 2030. Up to 2030, the bank will continue supporting customers’ transition and exit strategies. Exposure is defined as holdings (credit and investment across CaixaBank, S.A. and BPI) in companies whose economic group is more than 5% dependent on thermal coal.
text:
Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
CaixaBank acknowledges the difficulty implicit in the decarbonisation of this 
sector, which leads it to consider a certain level of prudence in terms of the 
management margin for decarbonising the portfolio. Nonetheless, CaixaBank is 
also aware of the existence of certain levers for decarbonising its portfolio, which 
depend substantially on the ambition of its main customers. Through 
engagement and portfolio rebalancing processes, CaixaBank will pursue an 
intermediate target compatible with the 1.5 ºC target. Thus, the range set 
(reduction between 10% and 20%) expresses CaixaBank's ambition, given that it 
incorporates, in its low range, the arrival level determined by the IEA's NZE.

- The alignment metric shows a slight uptick versus the baseline, attributed to data quality issues, while CaixaBank remains committed to its 2030 phase‑out target.

- Commercial real estate (CRE) alignment approach:

Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
As part of the commitment undertaken, the Entity's transition plan for this sector 
consists in not approving and renewing any positions and/or operations at

Commercial real estate sector
Main design features of the alignment metric
The commercial real estate sector is a complex sector and, to date, the availability of 
actual emissions data remains limited, which is why the use of proxies in the 
alignment calculations is still important. In addition, it is a sector with relevant 
geographical variations, where the reference pathways can lead to substantial 
variations in the targets. 
In light of these circumstances, CaixaBank has set an ambitious target for the 
sector. Given the limited availability of actual information relating to the assets in 
portfolio in this sector, priority will be provided to improving the availability of 
EPCs and of information on emissions of assets in portfolio. 
It is particularly worth mentioning that meeting the set target is conditional upon 
meeting the energy efficiency and energy mix projections included in the current 
PNIEC (Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan) and other related 
projections (draft of the future PNIEC, Fit for 55, etc.).                                                                                                                                                                                              Management Report 2024

title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
heading: 1.6.3.4.6.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
start_phrase: The decarbonisation of the commercial real estate can be achieved by adding to the stock new buildings with better EPCs or by improving those of the current stock.
summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 41% reduction target in carbon intensity (kgCO2e/m2) for its commercial real estate portfolio by 2030, moving from a 2022 baseline of 20.5 to 12.1 by 2030.
- The metric remained largely stable from 2022 to 2023 (around a 2% decrease), reflecting reliance on proxy data; improving data quality—especially EPCs and asset emissions information—is a priority.
- Sector transition plan focuses on working with customers to decarbonize by:
  - Adding new buildings with better energy performance certificates (EPCs).
  - Retrofitting existing stock through improved insulation (façades, windows, envelopes), installing solar panels, and upgrading to more efficient HVAC systems.
  - Using enhanced data to finance both efficient new builds and renovation projects that lift energy performance.
- For residential real estate, the alignment metric is not initially tied to the CRREM pathway due to social sensitivity, long maturities, and dependence on regulatory and public-aid levers.
- CaixaBank will leverage policy changes, environmental regulations, and shifts in consumer behavior, and is launching specific products to finance energy-efficient home retrofits.
- The CRREM 1.5°C pathway is referenced as a benchmark, with CaixaBank’s own trajectory showing a planned decline toward 2030.
text:
Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
The decarbonisation of the commercial real estate can be achieved by adding to 
the stock new buildings with better EPCs or by improving those of the current 
stock.The improvements can involve increasing the thermal insulation by restoring the 
façades, windows and envelopes of buildings; installing solar panels; or replacing 
HVAC systems with more energy-efficient options. The first step to activate the 
levers for decarbonisation of CaixaBank's financed footprint in this sector is to 
increase the availability of EPCs and of information on the emissions of its assets 
in portfolio. 
With a better availability of information, the levers for decarbonisation of the 
commercial real estate's portfolio will be the financing of new buildings with 
better energy ratings and of restoration projects that improve the current stock's 
energy efficiency.

heading: 1.6.3.4.8.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030

summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s maritime sector decarbonization approach, target design, and measurement framework.
- Methodology: Uses the Poseidon Principles (adopted by CaixaBank in 2022) to calculate portfolio alignment.
- Metric: Alignment Delta (AD%) based on physical emissions intensity; measures how a ship/portfolio aligns with decarbonization trajectories.
- Scope of emissions: Scope 1 fuel combustion during shipping (most material for the sector).
- Value chain boundary: Owner/Operator (port-to-port cargo transfer), as the use phase accounts for ~92% of value-chain emissions.
- Reference pathway: IMO’s 2018 initial strategy (2°C-consistent; 50% emissions reduction by 2050 vs 2008), with updates pending under Poseidon.
- Coverage: Cargo ships only; passenger vessels (fast ferries, cruise ships) excluded due to methodological inconsistencies in current alignment paths.
- Baseline and targets:
  - 2022 baseline AD%: 11.9% (Poseidon Principles cargo benchmark; NZBA reference).
  - 2030 arrival level: AD% = 0% (full alignment).
  - Ambition by 2030: −11.9 percentage points improvement in AD%.
- Future work: Target design will be refined as the Poseidon Principles update methodologies and pathways.

heading: 1.6.3.4.8.2 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
start_phrase: The decarbonisation in the naval sector involves implementing clean propulsion technologies, such as electric motors or the use of wind or solar energy), and less polluting alternative fuels, such as liquefied natural gas, biofuels or ammonia.
summary:
- Naval sector transition actions:
  - Focus on decarbonising shipping via cleaner propulsion (electric, wind, solar) and lower-emission alternative fuels (LNG, biofuels, ammonia).
  - Inclusion of shipping in the EU Emissions Trading System expected to accelerate adoption of cleaner technologies.
  - CaixaBank’s main lever is customer engagement to promote more efficient vessels and technologies.
  - Portfolio management includes gradually reducing exposure to assets less aligned with the Poseidon Principles and potential derisking.

- Aviation sector alignment approach and targets:
  - Methodology: Aligned with the Pegasus standard.
  - Initial scope: Corporate financing of airlines; excludes Asset Finance and lessors due to limited asset-level data (aircraft type, cargo, flight hours, fuel). Scope to be expanded as data improves, with baseline and targets adjustable accordingly.
  - 2030 target: Reduce physical emissions intensity from 102 gCO2e/RPK (2022 baseline) to 71 gCO2e/RPK by 2030 (about a 30% reduction).
  - Value chain focus: Aircraft owners/operators (passenger and cargo), where >90% of emissions occur during operations.
  - Emissions scope: Scope 1, tank-to-wake (in-flight fuel combustion).
  - Metric: Physical intensity (gCO2e per RPK).
  - Decarbonisation pathway: Mission Possible Partnership “Prudent” 1.5°C scenario (MPPU 1.5°C), consistent with Pegasus.
  - Key design decisions structured around value chain, emissions scope, metric, and pathway selection.
text:
Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
The decarbonisation in the naval sector involves implementing clean propulsion 
technologies, such as electric motors or the use of wind or solar energy), and less 
polluting alternative fuels, such as liquefied natural gas, biofuels or ammonia.
The inclusion of this sector in the EU Emissions Trading System should accelerate 
the implementation of these cleaner technologies. In this context, CaixaBank's 
main lever for decarbonisation of the naval sector's portfolio is customer 
engagement, with the aim of promoting the use of more efficient vessels and 
technology. The gradual reduction of exposure to assets less aligned with the 
Poseidon Principles and, even, the deriskingof exposures is also considered.

start_phrase: The target for this sector was calculated in line with the Pegasus methodology, a standard to which CaixaBank has adhered.
summary:
Aviation sector
Main design features of the alignment metric
The target for this sector was calculated in line with the Pegasus methodology, a 
standard to which CaixaBank has adhered. 
Initially, the scope focuses on the corporate financing of airlines, excluding Asset 
Finance and lessors, given the limited availability of technical data at individual 
asset level: type of aircraft, type of cargo, flight hours, type of fuel, etc. 
CaixaBank will extend the scope of the metric to these assets to the extent that 
the information becomes available, so it is foreseeable that the baseline and the 
level of arrival will also be adapted.CaixaBank's target by 2030
text:
Aviation sector
Main design features of the alignment metric
The target for this sector was calculated in line with the Pegasus methodology, a 
standard to which CaixaBank has adhered. 
Initially, the scope focuses on the corporate financing of airlines, excluding Asset 
Finance and lessors, given the limited availability of technical data at individual 
asset level: type of aircraft, type of cargo, flight hours, type of fuel, etc. 
CaixaBank will extend the scope of the metric to these assets to the extent that 
the information becomes available, so it is foreseeable that the baseline and the 
level of arrival will also be adapted.

title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
heading: 1.6.3.4.9.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
start_phrase: A reduction target for the AD% by 2030 intensity is established at 11.9%, with the following characteristics:
summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s sector transition plan, highlighting customer engagement actions to decarbonise shipping (naval) and aviation portfolios.
- Naval sector:
  - Transition levers: adoption of cleaner propulsion (electric, wind, solar) and alternative fuels (LNG, biofuels, ammonia).
  - Policy driver: inclusion of maritime in the EU Emissions Trading System expected to accelerate clean technology uptake.
  - Banking approach: engage customers to promote more efficient vessels/technologies; gradually reduce exposure to assets misaligned with the Poseidon Principles and consider derisking.
- Aviation sector:
  - Alignment framework: targets set using the Pegasus methodology; reference pathway is Mission Possible Partnership “Prudent” 1.5°C (MPPU 1.5°C).
  - Scope: initially limited to corporate financing of airlines (excluding asset finance and lessors) due to limited asset-level data; intent to expand scope as data improves, with potential updates to baseline and targets.
  - Emissions boundary: Scope 1 (tank-to-wake) in-flight fuel consumption, the most material source in the value chain.
  - Metric: physical emissions intensity in gCO2e per revenue passenger kilometre (gCO2e/RPK).
  - Target: reduce intensity by 2030 from a 2022 baseline of 102 gCO2e/RPK to 71 gCO2e/RPK (indicative −30%); document also references an 11.9% AD% reduction metric.
  - Value chain focus: owners/operators (passenger and cargo airlines), where >90% of sector emissions occur during aircraft operation.

title: Evolution of the metric
heading: 1.6.3.4.9.2 Evolution of the metric
start_phrase: The aviation metric slightly rises due to the cancellation of certain less intensive positions.
summary:
- Aviation sector: The portfolio’s aviation emissions metric shows a slight rise driven by the cancellation of lower-intensity positions. CaixaBank plans to broaden the scope to include additional material assets, which may alter future results. Decarbonisation priorities focus on sustainable aviation fuels (SAF) and more efficient aircraft technologies. CaixaBank’s levers are customer engagement to promote cleaner technologies, fleet renewal toward more efficient aircraft, and potential reduction of certain exposures.

- Agriculture and livestock sector: CaixaBank conducted an in-depth analysis of its portfolio to segment by materiality and carbon intensity, identify information gaps, and account for heterogeneous decarbonisation pathways across products. Given immature global methodologies and limited comparable data, a quantitative target is not yet set.

- Emissions scope and value chain: The most emissions-intensive stage is production; livestock (especially pigs and cattle) drives most emissions in the portfolio. Companies are treated as integrated across production, processing, distribution, and marketing. Included emissions cover on-farm sources (enteric fermentation, manure management, energy use) and feed production.

- Alignment metric and pathway: The chosen metric is physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e per kg of meat), aligned with SBTi FLAG. The reference pathway is SBTi FLAG Commodity Pathways consistent with a 1.5°C trajectory.

- GHG coverage: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, and NF3 are included.
text:
Evolution of the metric
The aviation metric slightly rises due to the cancellation of certain less intensive 
positions. However, as explained in previous paragraphs, work is being carried 
out on including the rest of material assets in the metric, which will involve 
changes in subsequent publications.

title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
heading: 1.6.3.4.9.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
start_phrase: The priority in the decarbonisation of the aviation sector is the use of sustainable fuels (SAF) and the implementation of more efficient technologies in the aircraft.
summary:
- Aviation sector metric: slight increase noted, driven by the cancellation of less intensive positions; upcoming methodology refinement will add remaining material assets, implying future changes to reported figures.
- Aviation decarbonisation approach: prioritises sustainable aviation fuels (SAF) and more efficient aircraft technologies; CaixaBank’s levers are customer engagement to promote cleaner technologies, fleet renewal toward higher efficiency, and potential reduction of certain exposures.
- Agriculture and livestock sector framework: comprehensive portfolio analysis conducted to segment by materiality and carbon intensity, identify data gaps, and recognise heterogeneous decarbonisation pathways across products; due to immature global methodologies and limited comparable data, no quantitative target is set yet.
- Emissions focus and value chain: production is the most emissions-intensive stage; pigs and cattle dominate the portfolio’s emissions; companies are treated as integrated across production, processing, distribution, and marketing.
- Emissions scope: includes on-farm emissions (enteric fermentation, manure management, energy use) and feed production—covering the majority of sector emissions.
- Metric and pathway: adopts a physical intensity metric (kgCO2e per kg of meat produced) aligned with SBTi FLAG; reference pathway is SBTi FLAG Commodity Pathways for 1.5°C alignment.
- Design decisions: define value chain boundaries (integrated companies), include direct emissions (on-farm and feed), and use a physical intensity metric.
- Additional notes: visuals compare CaixaBank’s metric trend with a 1.5°C pathway; CO2e coverage includes CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, and NF3.
text:
Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
The priority in the decarbonisation of the aviation sector is the use of sustainable 
fuels (SAF) and the implementation of more efficient technologies in the aircraft. 
In this context, CaixaBank's levers for decarbonisation of the aviation sector's 
portfolio will be customer engagement, with the aim of promoting the 
implementation of less polluting technologies, the stock's renewal with more 
efficient aircraft and the eventual reduction of certain exposures.

> Identify the main information gaps.
> Understand the heterogeneity of the paths for the products in the portfolio.

title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
heading: 1.6.3.4.10.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
start_phrase: A qualitative target focused on improving the knowledge and profiling of individual customers and the sector in general has been established.
summary:
- Sets a qualitative 2030 target to improve knowledge and profiling of individual customers and the sector overall.
- Launches a 2024 action plan focused on engaging main pork and beef customers to gather detailed information over 12 months, with milestones:
  - Identify key clients and define questionnaires; set internal targets.
  - Implement a meeting plan and agree measurement targets with customers.
  - Conclude the exercise, evaluate results, and reassess whether to set a quantitative target.
- States very low exposure to cement and aluminium sectors (<1% of total corporate credit/financed emissions).
- Because these sectors are non-material under NZBA, no decarbonisation targets are set for them.
- Establishes a monitoring and contingency plan: track relative exposure; if any of these sectors exceeds 1% of the non-financial corporate portfolio for three consecutive months, consider setting a Net Zero target.

title: Cement and aluminium sectors
heading: 1.6.3.4.11 Cement and aluminium sectors
start_phrase: The Entity's aggregate exposure to the cement and aluminium sectors, both in terms of credit exposure and absolute financed issues, does not exceed 1% of the bank's total portfolio of companies with a credit profile.
summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 2030 qualitative target to enhance knowledge and profiling of individual customers and the sector, with a 12-month engagement plan focused on major pork and beef clients.
- 2024 action plan:
  - Phase 01: Identify key clients; prepare a questionnaire on key topics; set internal targets.
  - Phase 02: Execute a meeting plan; agree measurement targets with customers.
  - Phase 03: Conclude and evaluate results; reassess the feasibility of a quantitative target.
- For cement and aluminium sectors:
  - Aggregate exposure is below 1% of the total corporate credit portfolio; considered non-material under NZBA.
  - No decarbonisation targets will be set for these sectors.
  - A monitoring and contingency plan will track relative exposure; if any sector exceeds 1% for three consecutive months, the bank will consider setting a Net Zero target.
text:
Cement and aluminium sectors  
The Entity's aggregate exposure to the cement and aluminium sectors, both in 
terms of credit exposure and absolute financed issues, does not exceed 1% of 
the bank's total portfolio of companies with a credit profile. Given the non-NZBA 
materiality of these sectors, it has been determined: 
> Not to set decarbonisation targets for the cement and aluminium sectors. 
> Establish a monitoring and contingency plan:
> Monitor a relative exposure metric: should the individual exposure of 
any of the sectors represent more than 1% of the total portfolio of non-
financial companies for three consecutive months, consideration will be 
given to addressing the setting of the Net Zero target. 
                                                                                                                                                                                              Management Report 2024

title: Calculation of financed CO2e emissions - Introduction
heading: 1.6.4 Calculation of financed CO2e emissions
start_phrase: CaixaBank quantifies the emissions related to its financing and investment (category 15 of Scope 3 of the carbon footprint), in order to understand, assess and manage the impact of its financial activity regarding its carbon footprint and the transitions risks linked to climate change.
summary: Introduces CaixaBank’s approach to quantifying financed CO2e emissions (Scope 3, category 15) to assess its carbon footprint and transition risks and to inform decarbonisation pathways aligned with NZBA net‑zero by 2050, using PCAF’s Global GHG Accounting & Reporting Standard. Defines the calculation perimeter across CaixaBank Group entities (CaixaBank, CPC, Bank BPI) and, as of 31 December 2024, covers loan portfolio assets including mortgages, commercial real estate (CRE), corporate loans, project finance, and vehicle financing; for CPC, only corporate loans, vehicle financing, and sovereign debt are included. Extends to the investment portfolio (corporate bonds, sovereign debt, equities) with practically 100% hedge and excludes the trading book. Notes first‑time estimation in 2024 of emissions linked to the sovereign debt asset per PCAF (includes bonds and financing to countries on the balance sheet, covering supranational loans and bonds and excluding sovereign bonds and loans); sovereign debt results appear in the “GHG emissions from the financing and investment portfolio – 2024” table and include CaixaBank and CPC (not BPI). Reports perimeter coverage of 86% exposure calculated and 14% not calculated due to insufficient data.
text:
Calculation of financed CO2e emissions  
CaixaBank quantifies the emissions related to its financing and investment 
(category 15 of Scope 3 of the carbon footprint), in order to understand, assess 
and manage the impact of its financial activity regarding its carbon footprint and 
the transitions risks linked to climate change.
In addition, this information assists CaixaBank  in defining decarbonisation 
pathways  to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, in keeping with the 
commitment of the NZBA. CaixaBank takes as a reference the guidelines set out 
by PCAF1 (Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials) in its accounting and 
reporting standard "The global GHG accounting & reporting standard for the 
financial industry" when quantifying the emissions financed by its loan and 
investment portfolio .
The calculation of the CaixaBank Group's financed emissions includes the main 
companies that carry out the Group's financing activity: CaixaBank, CPC and 
Bank BPI.
The calculation for the loan portfolio at 31 December 2024 covers the following 
types of assets2: 
> Mortgages 
> Commercial real estate (CRE3) 
> Corporate loans 
> Project Finance 
> Loans for financing vehiclesPerimeter loan portfolio. Hedge
Additionally, the financed emissions linked to the investment portfolio4 (including 
corporate bonds, sovereign debt and equities) have been calculated, establishing 
a hedge of practically 100%. In 2024 the emissions linked to the sovereign debt 
asset4, which according to the PCAF standard includes bonds and financing to 
countries5 in the Entity's balance sheet (covering supranational loans and bonds 
and excluding sovereign bonds and loans)6, has been estimated for the first time.
